simple.meaning: תְּחוֹת (tᵉchôwth) is a Hebrew word meaning “beneath.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: תְּחוֹת (H8460) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Jeremiah 10:11, with occurrences in Jeremiah, Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּחוֹת (H8460) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in תְּחוֹת (H8460) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: תְּחוֹת (tᵉchôwth) / H8460 is traced through Jeremiah 10:11, Daniel 4:9, Daniel 4:18, Daniel 7:27 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’ ”

timeline.evidenceText: “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’ ”

“Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation.

“This dream I, king Nebuchadnezzar, have seen; and you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able; for the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”

The kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole sky, will be given to the people of the saints of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey him.’

definitions.full: H8460. techoth תְּחוֺת preposition under (Biblical Hebrew תַּחַתּ ; תְּחוֺת ᵑ7 , Syriac , , adverb ; Palmyrene לתחת מן Cooke 320 ); — Dan 7:27 כָּלשְֿׁמַיָּא תְּחוֺת (compare Biblical Hebrew II. 1 ); in plural with suffix (as Biblical Hebrew, Syriac, ᵑ7 ) 4:9 תְּחֹתֹהִי (so ᵑ7 Onk Lev 15:10 : Dalm § 47, 2 ), 15:18 . With מִן , Jer 10:11 שְׁמַיָּא תְּחוֺת מִן (compare Biblical Hebrew III. 2 ); suffix Dan 4:11 מִןתַּֿחְתּוֺהִי (the form as Syriac adverb above, unless a Hebraizing punct.).
